messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: <long double> issue
parts:
Anyone know what's up with this?

"Exception thrown at line 82: Error in function boost::math::lgamma<long double>(long double): Evaluation of lgamma at 0."

It was a message reported by Swupnil Sahai on stan-users.
I followed up, and he says he has a 2014 Macbook Pro, so I
have no idea what a long double is doing in there.

If nobody knows, I'll try to recreate the report on my machine
and file an issue.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] <long double> issue

If you can set up the test case, we can track that down pretty quickly.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] <long double> issue
parts:
On Thursday, May 5, 2016 at 12:10:02 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Sorry, my issue was with how the type ***long double*** got into
the mix.  We shouldn't be using that anywhere.  And given recent
speed reports, I'm wondering if this is somehow negatively impacting
the speed of Stan code.

Macs have been using libc++ as their C++ library for a while, regardless of whether C++11 is specified as the standard. So, it may just be doing what it would do under C++11 where a long double is well-defined.

Ben
